# Stage 3: the core screens and journeys

The core screens, so a person can do every core journey: check in, read a goal, see what needs attention, run a review.

**Today:** drill ready: the harness scores part of it against the conformance data. The rest of its exit criteria are checked by hand.

## Entry criteria

- Stage 2 passes its exit criteria.

## What to read

- [The screens](../core/screens.md): each core route, its purpose, named parts and one main action, and its fields, states and buttons; then the views and overlays with no route of their own.
- [The design rules](../core/design-rules.md): the look. [The Help guide](../core/help-guide.md): what each screen is for and who can, in full.
- [The journeys](../core/journeys.md): what people do end to end, the most steps each may take, and the ease test; then each journey’s own page (`core/journeys/<id>.md`, linked from its Id): where it starts and as whom, every step (what to press or type, by the words on the screen) and every check (what must then be visible or saved). A step is one press or one field typed into; the budget counts those.
- [The requirements](../core/requirements.md): each one, with the screens and Help article that cover it.
- [Goals’ filters and sort](../core/goals-query.md): what each filter and sort in a Goals link means, its values and its words.
- [The vocabulary](../core/vocabulary.md): where each word may appear. A status is always a shape and a word.

## What to build

- Each core screen at its route, with its named parts and one main action at a time.
- Every core journey, within its step budget, on a phone (390px) and a desktop (1440px).
- A goal’s page in one order at every width: the summary and its buttons, Next steps and asks, Why, the chart, then the rest. Its main button is a rule of who is looking ([acting on a goal](../core/rules/goal-act.md)), not a layout choice; Next steps and asks is one query over the goal’s asks and next steps; someone acting for the owner (R6b) presses the owner’s buttons for them.
- One find-and-pick control wherever a person, team or goal is chosen (requirement `FIND-AND-PICK`): the choice in words with Change, suggestions before typing ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md), rule 6), then a search through the `Search` port, its count, at most 50 rows, arrow keys, Enter and Escape. Never a list of everyone: the server’s search plugs in behind the port.
- Find from anywhere (requirement `FIND-ANYWHERE`): the sidebar’s Find, the phone’s Find button and Ctrl K (Cmd K) open one search across goals, people, teams and a module’s kinds, drawn in groups of three with “See all {n} {things}”, a key’s goal alone and first, and Enter opening the first row ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md), rule 8). Each group is one call to the `Search` port, so the server’s search answers it.
- One list bar on every list (requirement `LIST-BAR`): the search, then the count line, the filter line and what found nothing in [finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)’ words; the list’s search and filters in the address, a choice adding a history entry. The server pages the list (R4).
- The menu, the lit item and a page’s name as three rules of the viewer and the address ([navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md)), drawn by the shell: a module adds a menu item in a group, names its pages from their thing, and fills places on a goal’s, a person’s and a team’s page.
- Where you are (requirements `NAV-WHERE`, `NAV-BACK`, `NAV-FORMS`): the browser’s title is the page’s own name by rule 2; one back link per page by rule 4, which goes back in the tab’s history (stepping over forms) so it agrees with the browser’s Back, and up to the parent when there is no history; a form’s one closing control in words, asking first before throwing typed words away.
- New goal and the first check-in keep day one honest ([a goal not born late](../core/rules/not-born-late.md)): a stage already past is asked about and, if done, recorded done in its own week; a first number off the plan may restart it. These are rules, with the status rules, not screen details.
- New goal in four steps, each an address ([New goal](../core/rules/new-goal.md)): what, who and where, how it’s measured, check. Its level and the suggestions for what it feeds are rules. In the internal app New goal becomes R6c’s draft-and-propose, and owners and teams come from the directory (R2).
- Its last step is the read-back ([the read-back](../core/rules/read-back.md)): the goal in sentences (What, Who and where, Measured by, Left as usual, You said), each with Change to its step and Continue straight back, then “After you publish”: the first check-in’s day, who sees it, the reviews it joins (`reviewsJoining`) and how long it can be taken back. A rule, so the internal app’s form and its draft-and-propose say the same.
- One set of rules at every door ([goal entry](../core/rules/goal-entry.md)): New goal, the edit page, set-up’s goal cards, a spreadsheet’s Goals rows and the AI tools ask the same `goalMustFix`, in the same words, and the form saves through the `saveGoal` command, never by itself, so nothing the change engine would refuse is saved. Anyone may add a goal for anyone at any level; only its owner or an admin changes it. The questions (`goalChecks`, rule 3) are asked the same way: possible but unlikely values (over 100%, below zero, a hundredfold, a billion, no unit, a wide margin, a late hand-set plan, the same name in the same team, an owner in another team, a link to a lower level, a stage already past) are a Check under their field, answered once for the values they are about and kept in History as Checked; Continue and the save wait for them, and the AI tools list them and take `confirm`. Both belong with the status rules in stage 1’s conformance data; until then the change engine’s cases in `import.csv` carry them (`has-words`, `same-as-start`, `stage-twice`, a goal added for someone else, `over-100-and-hundredfold`, `margin-wide`, `feeds-lower`).
- A goal’s weeks are picked, never typed (requirement `GOAL-DATES`; [years and weeks](../core/rules/years-and-weeks.md)): a number goal’s Baseline with its From and Target with its To, and a stage’s Due, each chosen from a short list of a goal year’s weeks with their dates, opened at the chosen week, with up to three named weeks. The data keeps weeks counted from the cycle’s start; one rule converts, and the sheet and the AI tools write `2026-W46`. A plan whose From is still to come is not due until then. The change engine’s cases in `import.csv` carry the sheet’s side (`to-before-from`, `week-unknown`, `from-pair-disagrees`, `to-next-year`).
- Change a goal is one page (requirement `GOAL-EDIT-PAGE`): four sections an address opens at (`#definition`, `#plan`, `#owner`, then More details), its one closing control “Close and keep the draft”, Save changes held at the window’s foot, and old `?part=` links led to the matching section. A plan change after check-ins have started needs a reason; that is the plan-change rule, not the page’s.
- **The module platform** ([the module platform](module-platform.md)), with no module in it: every place on the core screens built empty (a core screen draws whatever the modules that are on put there, and nothing when none does), a route, a menu row in a group, a Workspace section, a Help article and an AI tool registered from a module’s facts, `Workspace.modulesOff` and the rule of which modules are on, Workspace → Features with its groups, switches and read-backs, every sentence the core says while a module is off, and the AI tools’ server with its methods, batches, refusals and dry runs, answering the core’s own tools. Every module stage after this one only registers into it.
- Goals’ layouts (requirement `GOALS-MENUS`; [the Help guide](../core/help-guide.md), Goals): the Layout menu at the end of the list bar (“Layout: List”; “View: List” on a phone) with the core’s four layouts, List, Table, Board and History, the layout in the link and remembered; a module adds a layout to the same menu (the Goal map). Each layout reads the same goals through the query port ([Goals’ filters and sort](../core/goals-query.md)), and a group of goals is summed up by one status, the worst ([the status](../core/rules/status.md), “A group’s status”).

## The drill

Stage 3’s drill scores the parts of the screens that are rules of the viewer, the address and the workspace, not of the markup: the menu, the lit item and a page’s name for two viewers at each address (`navigation.csv`), what New goal’s last step reads back for six drafts (`readback.csv`), what a search for a goal, a person or a team finds and in what order (`find.csv`), and Home’s lead or quiet line for four viewers over fourteen days (`home.csv`). Each is a function a screen calls, so a rebuild can pass it before drawing anything.

- `rebuild/drill.json` holds `{ "stage": 3, "run": "<command>" }`. The harness runs it as stage 1’s ([the contract](stage-1-core-rules.md#the-contract)): `<command> <workspace.json> <out folder>`, a copy of `spec/conformance/workspace.json` and `rebuild/drill-out/`, emptied first.
- The command writes these files into the out folder and exits 0, within 10 minutes:

| File | Rows expected | Columns, in this order |
|---|---|---|
| `navigation.csv` | 60 | `viewer`, `owns_goals`, `address`, `menu`, `tabs`, `lit`, `page` |
| `readback.csv` | 6 | `case`, `viewer`, `draft`, `rows`, `after` |
| `find.csv` | 23 | `kind`, `q`, `total`, `near`, `ids` |
| `home.csv` | 56 | `viewer`, `day`, `lead`, `title`, `quiet`, `run`, `forgiven` |

- **The cases’ inputs** are in [`screen-cases.json`](../conformance/screen-cases.json), and the harness puts a copy of it beside the `workspace.json` it hands the command (the same folder), as it does stage 2’s `change-cases.json`: the workspace’s name as the screens say it, the viewers and addresses `navigation.csv` answers (with a module’s menu item, and Home with features switched off), every search `find.csv` makes, the drafts `readback.csv` reads back (each set over the `blank` goal it gives, the draft’s every field), and Home’s viewers and moments. Read the cases from there, never from the expected files: in each CSV the inputs are written back, and its key columns are among them (navigation.csv’s `viewer` and `address`, find.csv’s `kind` and `q`, home.csv’s `viewer` and `day`; readback.csv’s is its `case` alone, with the case’s `viewer` and `draft` beside it), and every other column is what the screens’ rules give. What each column holds, word for word, is in [the conformance data](../conformance/README.md#the-files). Rows are matched by their key columns, columns by name, text exactly.

### A good order

1. [Navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md): `navigation.csv` (`--files navigation`).
2. [Finding things](../core/rules/finding.md): `find.csv`.
3. [Home](../core/rules/home.md): `home.csv`.
4. [The read-back](../core/rules/read-back.md): `readback.csv`, which needs [New goal](../core/rules/new-goal.md)’s level and [goal entry](../core/rules/goal-entry.md)’s questions.

**What the drill doesn’t prove:** the screens themselves, their layout and look, and the journeys (exit criteria 2 to 4).

## Exit criteria

1. `node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild` prints **PASS** with `"stage": 3`: every row and column of `navigation.csv`, `readback.csv`, `find.csv` and `home.csv` match.
2. Each core journey in [the journeys](../core/journeys.md) can be done within its budget, by hand, on both widths: its page’s steps, in order, from where it starts, with every check on it true.
3. Each core requirement in [the requirements](../core/requirements.md) holds.
4. No screen offers a person, team or goal from a list of everything (Faro checks it with `scripts/check-pickers.mjs`; the places it still allows are listed in `scripts/pickers-left.json`).
5. `node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --expected spec/conformance/core-only` prints **PASS** too: the same four files on the same workspace with every feature module switched off (`modulesOff`), so the core is proved without any module ([the core alone](../conformance/README.md#the-core-alone-core-only)). Leave `drill.json` as it is: a file or contract `core-only/` doesn’t hold (it has these four files and no `contracts/`) is named once as not scored, so `also` and `contracts` carried from stage 2 can stay.
6. The module platform holds what [its page](module-platform.md#what-proves-it-stage-3s-exit-criterion-for-the-platform) lists, with one example module on, switched off and left out.

## Gaps in the kit

Where the kit doesn’t yet hold what this stage needs, so a rebuild would have to guess:

- The journeys are driven by Faro’s own eval scripts against Faro’s own markup (`evals/journeys.cjs`), which are not in the kit and would not run against another build. Each journey’s steps and checks are in the kit in words, read from that code ([the journeys](../core/journeys.md#how-to-read-a-journeys-steps)), so a rebuild knows what each one does; but nothing runs them against a rebuild: there is no portable journey runner yet, so they are done by hand. Where a step names a part only by Faro’s CSS class, the words beside it say what it is.
- The look is in [the design rules](../core/design-rules.md) and the Help guide in full in [the Help guide](../core/help-guide.md); each screen’s fields, states and buttons are read from Faro’s markup ([the screens](../core/screens.md)), with words worked out when it shows written “…” and the conditions a button shows under as Faro’s code writes them. Each screen has two pictures (390 and 1440 wide) of Faro as it is; they are taken by hand with `npm run spec:shots`, so a change to a screen can leave its picture a step behind until the next run.
- Faro’s mark (the F’s stem, beam and bar, and “aro”) is drawn from paths in `src/ui/brandPaths.ts`, which are not in the kit: the home-screen icon and the launch splash (requirement `LAUNCH`) are described in words, so a rebuild draws its own mark to them.
- Some screens the journeys step through are named in the journeys but not yet described in [the screens](../core/screens.md) beyond their markup: set-up, and the year’s start and end. Their journey pages are the fullest words for them today. (Saved views, the step-by-step check-in and a first check-in’s offer to start the plan from its number now have their own rows there: Goals: the View sheet, and Check-in: one goal, a step at a time.)
